decision.summary: The Fed held its policy rate at 0% to 0.25%. The vote was 8-1. Dissenting: Jeffrey M. Lacker.

changes.quote: The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to keep its target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “The Federal Open Market Committee decided today to establish a target range for the federal funds rate of 0 to 1/4 percent.”

changes.quote: The Committee continues to anticipate that economic conditions are likely to warrant exceptionally low levels of the federal funds rate for some time.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: Information received since the Committee met in December suggests that the economy has weakened further.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: Industrial production, housing starts, and employment have continued to decline steeply, as consumers and businesses have cut back spending.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: Furthermore, global demand appears to be slowing significantly.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: Conditions in some financial markets have improved, in part reflecting government efforts to provide liquidity and strengthen financial institutions; nevertheless, credit conditions for households and firms remain extremely tight.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

The Committee continues to anticipate that economic conditions are likely to warrant exceptionally low levels of the federal funds rate for some time.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 11.94% APR costs about $49.75 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 2.71% and moved +12 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 4.96% would rise by about $22.03 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 7.3%, and employers added an average of -638k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was -0% over the past year (December 2008); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.1%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a -8.5% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +2 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.62% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is dovish (leaning toward lower rates). The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 25%, cut 75%, hike 0%.
